purpose: Check that ambiguous consequential work is framed before execution.
positivePrompts: Replacing billing could affect customers and operations, but the outcome is unclear and risky; frame the problem before implementation.
This request is ambiguous but high impact. Help me scope the work first.

cases.prompt: We might replace our billing integration and need to decide how to proceed.
checks: Identifies product goal, user impact, technical context, constraints, risks, stakeholders, and decision horizon.
Pressure-tests fuzzy terms, edge cases, contradictions, and hidden tradeoffs without turning scoping into a long interview.
Asks only the current blocking frontier, defers dependent questions, or states safe assumptions.
Converts scoped context into a next useful action.

cases.prompt: We may replace our billing provider, but we have not decided whether the goal is fewer payment failures, more international payment methods, or lower cost. Help me scope the decision. Provider selection, data migration, and rollout details may matter later, but do not turn this into an exhaustive interview or ask me for facts you can inspect yourself.
checks: Treats the product goal as an upstream decision that must be settled before downstream provider, migration, or rollout choices.
Asks only the current blocking frontier and explicitly defers questions whose answers depend on the unsettled goal.
Includes a recommended answer when it materially helps the user decide without pretending the user has accepted it.
Keeps the questioning bounded and owns discoverable facts instead of delegating research back to the user.

traceExpectations: Questions are limited to those that can change scope, design, rollout, or risk.
Dependent questions wait until their prerequisite decisions are settled.
Risks include product, architecture, security/privacy, operations, cost, and team speed.
